title: Block close: reason and faith
hookLine: Maimonides shows reason can serve faith
last: STUDY IS GREATER BECAUSE IT LEADS TO DEED.

cards: An epitaph that says none like Moses. A commentary on the Mishnah. A list of principles of faith.
Chapters on the health of the soul, and a middle way. A code of law in clear Hebrew. The rungs of giving.
A path of return. A picture of the messianic age. A guide for the perplexed, with silence as praise.
Then the arguments, the son, the honest reading, the grave by the lake. One question sits underneath it all: can a mind that asks hard questions still stand before God?

teach.b: Block close: reason and faith. First, reason is part of obeying. The Torah says the nations will hear these laws and call Israel "a wise and understanding people."
Maimonides leans on that verse in the Guide: if outsiders can see the wisdom, the commandments must have reasons a mind can look for. Thinking isn't a threat to the law. It's one way of honoring it.
Second, reason clears the way. You saw him do it with God's hand and God's eye: figures of speech, he said, not a body. And with praise: sometimes the truest thing a mind can offer is silence.
Reason sweeps away wrong pictures so a truer reverence has room.
Third, reason knows its edge. About the messianic age he said nobody will know how until it happens. About God he said we know better what God is not.

teach.h: REASON ENDS IN LOVE AND DEED.
teach.b: Fourth, reason ends in love and in deed. His code says a person who looks at the wonders of creation is moved to love and to awe, and his Guide ends with kindness, justice and righteousness.
For Maimonides, thinking isn't the opposite of faith. It's one of the ways faith is served.
Not everyone agreed, then or now: you met the Rabad's sharp notes, and the Ramban's other way, toward a hidden layer in the Torah.
Tomorrow a new block begins with that hidden layer: the tradition called Kabbalah, a different road into the same Torah.

how: Jews study Maimonides' code and his Guide in yeshivas, universities and study groups, and his principles of faith appear in prayer books in the hymn Yigdal and the Ani Ma'amin.

the start of a new study of the Talmud's laws

Maimonides says reason can tell where its knowing stops
about the messianic age and about God, he marks the edge of what we know.
every Jewish thinker accepted his approach
the Rabad argued in the margin, and the Ramban pointed toward a hidden layer of the Torah.

games.q: a student asks Maimonides: if I think hard about God, won't I lose my faith? what is his answer?
o: thinking, done carefully, is one way of serving faith.
faith doesn't matter if you can think.
games.why: he wrote the Guide for exactly that student: reason clears away wrong pictures, knows its edge, and ends in love and deed.

practice: Pick one question you've been carrying, about faith, a choice or a person, and think it through slowly, the way Maimonides liked: what do I actually know, and what am I only picturing?
When you reach the edge of what you can know, stop there, and let the rest be quiet.
